name: Run-D.M.C.
hook: Took the band off rap records, left only a drum machine, two voices and a DJ, and made that the new sound of the form.
blurb: Joseph Simmons, Darryl McDaniels and Jason Mizell (Jam Master Jay) came from Hollis, Queens. Before them, most rap records followed the Sugar Hill model: a label's house band replaying disco and funk behind acts the label put together. Their first single in 1983, produced by Larry Smith and Russell Simmons, had only a drum machine and their two voices trading lines. It sounded hard and bare, and it made the earlier style sound old. They also changed rap's look from party costumes to street clothes. In 1986 their version of Aerosmith's 'Walk This Way', with the rock band playing on it, reached number four on the Billboard Hot 100 and put rap on rock radio and MTV. The group ended in 2002 when Jam Master Jay was shot and killed in his Queens studio in October. The case went unsolved for more than twenty years, until two men were convicted of his murder in 2024.
